subject.title: WhatsApp 1:1: inbound image wedges main lane ~3min before processing — multimodal run strands active_reply_work/queued_work_without_active_run (repro on 2026.6.10, post-#95039)

question: Should stale `active_reply_work` after terminal-looking reply runs be reclaimed immediately for queued channel lanes, or should OpenClaw keep the current abort-threshold gate and only harden the owner-boundary cleanup?
rationale: The bug is real, but the safe recovery policy trades off user-visible message delay against aborting legitimate long-running work, and current main already contains partial mitigation without live WhatsApp proof.

options.title: Fix owner-boundary cleanup
options.body: Prefer clearing stale reply-run ownership when the run/session is terminal or proven orphaned, while keeping the conservative abort threshold for genuinely active work.

options.title: Lower recovery threshold
options.body: Treat the reported workaround as product policy and reclaim more quickly, accepting a higher risk of interrupting slow but valid runs.

options.title: Wait for live proof on main
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer or reporter validates current main against WhatsApp direct and group recurrence before deciding whether more code is needed.

recommendation.title: Fix owner-boundary cleanup
recommendation.body: Prefer clearing stale reply-run ownership when the run/session is terminal or proven orphaned, while keeping the conservative abort threshold for genuinely active work.

likelyOwner.reason: The current recovery and registry code involved in the policy choice is blamed to this recent area contributor.
